summary.short: Amends Ley 26.485 to define digital and telematic violence against women, add digital rights and digital literacy duties, and let courts order alleged aggressors to avoid digital contact and platforms to remove content and preserve data for 90 days. Entry-into-force date not stated.
summary.long: Amends Ley 26.485 on protection of women from violence. Adds digital rights to its objectives and dignity principle, and extends the definition of violence against women to acts committed or aggravated with information and communication technologies, in analog or digital space. Digital violence covers non-consensual distribution of real or edited intimate material, misogynist hate speech, harassment, threats, extortion, espionage and unauthorized access to accounts. It requires a free multi-channel reporting service, digital literacy in education, free judicial proceedings with digital forensic evidence, and protective orders: the alleged aggressor may be ordered to cease digital intimidation and to avoid contact through any technology. Courts may order platforms, social networks or websites, by reasoned order specifying the URL, to remove content and preserve traffic, subscriber and content data for 90 days, renewable once, with disclosure of subscriber data on request. The text states no penalties and no entry-into-force date; its dateline shows a publication notice dated 23/10/2023.
